title: Choosing a First Move
intro: Try starting near a corner, a few lines in from the edge. Your stones have room to grow, with two nearby board edges to help enclose territory.
These positions compare corners, sides and the centre. During a game, check threatened groups before following an opening plan.

steps.instruction: Choose a first move near a corner, a few lines in from the edge.
steps.hint: The four points a short step in from each corner are all good beginner starts.
steps.explanation: This stone has space around it and two nearby edges. It is one useful place to begin.

steps.instruction: Choose an opening point with more room than the first line.
steps.hint: Leave the first line alone for now. Pick a point near a corner with room on both sides.
steps.explanation: Points farther from the edge have more room to grow. First-line moves can still matter later for saving groups or closing boundaries.

steps.instruction: Close the gap in the corner wall, on the top edge.
steps.hint: Top edge, fourth line in from the left.
steps.explanation: Seven black stones surround nine corner points. Two sides of the boundary are the board edges.

steps.instruction: Close the gap in the wall along the side.
steps.hint: The bottom right of the wall you can see, on the fourth column.
steps.explanation: Eleven black stones surround nine points here. Only one board edge helps form the boundary.

steps.instruction: Close the gap in the centre wall.
steps.hint: The bottom right corner of the ring.
steps.explanation: Sixteen black stones surround nine points here. Black has to build the whole boundary.

outro: Corners are often an efficient place to start. Keep nearby stones connected and check for urgent threats before expanding.
